video.title: Child Task, Unstructured Task & Detached Task | Day 268
video.description:
Learn to explain the three ways to start a task and what each one inherits: Child Task, Unstructured Task & Detached Task, with real code, a quiz at the end and each example read twice (normal, then slow).

Today's terms
Child Task - A task that belongs to a parent task and ends before its parent does.
Unstructured Task - A task made with `Task { }` that is not tied to a parent scope but inherits the actor and priority of its creator.
Detached Task - A task that inherits nothing from its creator: not the actor, the priority or the task-local values.

Quiz at the end - write your answers in the comments, then watch again to check.

Explain Child Task, Unstructured Task & Detached Task in iOS by listening to a real code chat between two iOS devs.
Child Task, Unstructured Task, Detached Task 표현을 영어 대화로 익혀요.

Child Task - A task that belongs to a parent task and ends before its parent does.
한국어: Child Task: 부모 태스크에 속하며 부모보다 먼저 끝나는 태스크

Unstructured Task - A task made with `Task { }` that is not tied to a parent scope but inherits the actor and priority of its creator.
한국어: Unstructured Task: Task { }로 만들며 부모 범위에 묶이지 않지만 만든 쪽의 액터와 우선순위를 물려받는 태스크

Detached Task - A task that inherits nothing from its creator: not the actor, the priority or the task-local values.
한국어: Detached Task: 액터, 우선순위, 태스크 로컬 값 등 만든 쪽의 것을 아무것도 물려받지 않는 태스크

landscape.hook: Can you explain Child Task, Unstructured Task and Detached Task in English?

dialogue.title: Three ways to start work
dialogue.setting: A function that starts work in three ways

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Jake, I start work in three different ways in `run`. Which one is right?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Let us see. The first one, `async let`, makes a child task.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: A child task belongs to a parent task and ends before its parent does.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: That is an unstructured task. It is not tied to the parent scope, but it inherits the actor and priority.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: So if `run` ends, the unstructured task keeps going?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Yes, and you must cancel it yourself. A child task is cancelled with its parent.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: A detached task inherits nothing. No actor, no priority, no task-local values.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: I used a detached task for UI work, and the screen updated on the wrong thread.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: That is a common mistake. Use a detached task only when you really need a fresh start.
A child task ends before its parent.
